subject: history_social
passage: On December 12, 1901, Guglielmo Marconi sat in a room on Signal Hill in St. John's, Newfoundland, listening through an earpiece to a receiver attached to an antenna held aloft by a kite. He reported hearing three faint clicks, the letter S in Morse code, sent from a transmitter in Cornwall more than 3,000 kilometers ______ physicists at the time insisted that radio waves could not follow the curve of the Earth, so the claim met with doubt as well as excitement. Later experiments proved the principle, and regular transatlantic radio service began within a few years.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "He reported hearing three faint clicks … more than 3,000 kilometers away" is a complete sentence, and "many physicists at the time insisted that radio waves could not follow the curve of the Earth" is another. "However" is a transitional word, not a conjunction, so the two independent clauses need a semicolon before it and a comma after it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a comma after it, "However" reads as part of "However many physicists," which turns the second sentence into a fragment that never gets to its point.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma alone can't join two independent clauses; "however" is not a conjunction, so this is a comma splice.
explanation.C: Correct. A semicolon joins the two independent clauses, and commas set off the transitional word "however."
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation after "away," the two independent clauses run together.
